newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Farmer sales increase.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Farmer sales increase.

text.p: Farmer sales of hard red winter wheat have picked up over the last two days primarily because of a rally in U.S. wheat futures, grain merchandisers in the U.S. High Plains said Tuesday.
"I'd say we've bought twice as much wheat as normal over the last couplde of days," a south-central Kansas dealer said. "Farmers are just taking profits while they can."
Another south-central Kansas dealer said farmers were motivated to sell because they were coming up on the end of their 30-day free grain storage periods at local country elevators.
The dealer also said some farmers were trying to generate cash to pay off bills, specifically fertilizer bills.
Basis bids for HRW wheat in Kansas and Oklahoma were mostly unchanged.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: N=KCBT July. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
